title: Horizontal privilege escalation
content:
IDOR vulnerabilities are most commonly associated with horizontal privilege escalation, but they can also arise in relation to vertical privilege escalation.

With horizontal access controls, different users have access to a subset of resources of the same type.

When exploited, this weakness can result in authorization bypasses, horizontal privilege escalation and, less commonly, vertical privilege escalation (see CWE-639 ).

Horizontal access controls are mechanisms that restrict access to resources to specific users.

Such simplistic logic does a poor job of supporting object-level or horizontal access control decisions and those that require multiple factors.
